project.name: nisshi
project.description: Stateless, Apache Kafka-compatible broker written in Rust with pluggable storage backends (PostgreSQL, libSQL/SQLite, S3/object store, memory); schema-backed topics can be written as Apache Iceberg or Delta Lake tables.

nodes.languageNotes: SQLite-flavoured DDL using create table if not exists with autoincrement ids and cascade foreign keys.

nodes.name: topic_configuration

nodes.languageNotes: SQLite-flavoured DDL using create table if not exists with autoincrement ids and cascade foreign keys.

nodes.languageNotes: SQLite-flavoured DDL using create table if not exists with autoincrement ids and cascade foreign keys.

nodes.languageNotes: SQLite-flavoured DDL using create table if not exists with autoincrement ids and cascade foreign keys.

nodes.languageNotes: SQLite-flavoured DDL using create table if not exists with autoincrement ids and cascade foreign keys.

nodes.name: txn_detail
nodes.summary: Per-producer-epoch transaction state: timeout, start time and status for a transaction.
nodes.languageNotes: SQLite-flavoured DDL using create table if not exists with autoincrement ids and cascade foreign keys.

nodes.name: watermark
nodes.summary: Low and high watermark offsets for each topic-partition.
nodes.languageNotes: SQLite-flavoured DDL using create table if not exists with autoincrement ids and cascade foreign keys.

nodes.name: txn_offset_commit
nodes.summary: Offsets committed within a transaction for a consumer group, with generation and member id.
nodes.languageNotes: SQLite-flavoured DDL using create table if not exists with autoincrement ids and cascade foreign keys.

nodes.summary: Associates a transaction detail with the topic-partitions it has produced to.
nodes.languageNotes: SQLite-flavoured DDL using create table if not exists with autoincrement ids and cascade foreign keys.

nodes.summary: Reads SQLite's freelist page count and page size via pragma table functions, used to estimate reclaimable space.

nodes.name: policy_compact_compaction.sql
nodes.summary: Selects offset_ids of records for a topition and key that are older than a given offset, i.e. superseded entries to compact away.
nodes.languageNotes: SQLite dialect SQL with $N positional parameters.

nodes.name: policy_compact_delete.sql
nodes.summary: Deletes a single record row identified by topition and offset_id as part of log compaction.
nodes.languageNotes: SQLite dialect SQL with $N positional parameters.

nodes.name: policy_compact_distinct_k.sql
nodes.summary: Selects the distinct record keys present in a topition, the starting set for key-based compaction.
nodes.languageNotes: SQLite dialect SQL with $N positional parameters.

nodes.name: policy_compact_max_offset_id.sql
nodes.summary: Finds the latest offset_id for a given key within a topition, identifying the record compaction must keep.
nodes.languageNotes: SQLite dialect SQL with $N positional parameters.

nodes.name: policy_compact_topitions.sql
nodes.summary: Lists topition ids in a cluster whose topic cleanup.policy contains compact.
nodes.languageNotes: SQLite dialect SQL with $N positional parameters.

nodes.name: policy_delete.sql
nodes.summary: Deletes records older than each topic's retention.ms for delete-policy topics; a materialized CTE keeps SQLite from scanning all records, and non-numeric or negative retention values keep every record.
nodes.languageNotes: SQLite dialect SQL with $N positional parameters.

nodes.name: policy_delete_bytes.sql
nodes.summary: Enforces per-partition retention.bytes by deleting the oldest records once a running sum of key and value sizes exceeds the cap, always keeping the newest record.
nodes.languageNotes: SQLite dialect SQL with $N positional parameters.

nodes.name: vacuum_into.sql
nodes.summary: Runs SQLite VACUUM INTO a target path given as a parameter, producing a compacted copy of the database.
nodes.languageNotes: SQLite dialect SQL with $N positional parameters.

nodes.name: watermark_select_for_write.sql
nodes.summary: Selects the low and high watermarks and max.message.bytes for a topic partition; SQLite has no row locks so the write transaction's lock is used, and it mirrors the Postgres query's columns.
nodes.languageNotes: SQLite dialect SQL with $N positional parameters.

nodes.name: nisshi_schema_version_exists.sql
nodes.summary: Postgres query reading pg_class directly to tell whether the nisshi_schema_version table exists on the search path, avoiding the stale to_regclass cache so concurrent brokers do not create the schema twice.

nodes.name: record_fetch.sql
nodes.summary: Postgres fetch query that reads a capped window of records from a topition in offset order with a running byte total, returning rows under the byte limit and always the first row (KIP-74).

nodes.name: record_fetch_keyed.sql
nodes.summary: Variant of record_fetch that additionally filters records by an exact key match, with the row limit moved to parameter $8.

nodes.name: schema.sql
nodes.summary: Postgres DDL applied at broker startup: creates tables for clusters, topics, topitions, watermarks, partitioned records and headers, consumer groups and offsets, producers, transactions and SCRAM credentials, with indexes.

nodes.name: search_path_set_to_cluster_namespace.sql
nodes.summary: Postgres query that sets the transaction-local search_path to the namespace holding the cluster table, doing nothing in an empty database.

nodes.name: topic_configuration_select_keys.sql
nodes.summary: Postgres query returning the topic's values for a set of config keys, yielding a null-name row when the topic exists but sets none, so zero rows means the topic is missing.

nodes.name: topic_select_uuid.sql
nodes.summary: Postgres query resolving a topic by cluster name and UUID, unioning real topics with virtual topics keyed by their record key.

nodes.name: consumer_group_delete.sql
nodes.summary: Deletes a consumer group row identified by cluster name ($1) and group name ($2) via a subselect over cluster and consumer_group.

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Nisshi is a stateless Rust server that speaks the Apache Kafka API and stores data in a pluggable backend. The README covers installation, the Docker Compose setups for S3 (MinIO) and PostgreSQL, and the CLI subcommands. CLAUDE.md adds the intended architecture: the crate map, the sans-I/O code generation, and the build and test workflow. CLAUDE.md also has a "Checking Against Apache Kafka" section on how to verify behaviour against the reference implementation.

tour.title: One Binary, Many Subcommands
tour.description: The nisshi binary is the single entry point. It dispatches the subcommands (broker, cat, topic, user, generator, perf, proxy) and turns errors into actionable messages and exit codes. The nisshi-cli crate supplies the Clap-based argument parsing, including the EnvVarExp wrapper that expands ${VAR} references in arguments. missing_feature.rs rewrites clap's unknown-subcommand error to name the cargo feature (iceberg, delta, parquet) a lake subcommand needs when the binary was built without it.
tour.languageLesson: Rust workspaces split a product into many small crates under one Cargo.toml. Here the thin binary crate depends on library crates, so each tool (cat, topic, perf) can be tested and reused independently.

tour.title: The Workspace Manifest
tour.description: The root Cargo.toml lists every workspace member, shares package metadata and dependency versions, and sets the lint policy. It forbids unsafe code and denies broken doc links. Reading it gives you the crate inventory that the rest of the tour walks through.

tour.title: Generated Wire Protocol
tour.description: nisshi-sans-io holds the Kafka wire protocol as pure data types with no I/O. Its build.rs reads the upstream Kafka JSON message descriptors and generates the typed request and response structs, serde impls and arbitrary derives. lib.rs defines the Frame, Header and ErrorCode types that every later layer passes around.
tour.languageLesson: A sans-I/O design keeps protocol encoding and decoding free of sockets, so the same types serve the broker, client, proxy and fuzzers. A build.rs script generates code at compile time, so the generated files should never be edited by hand.

tour.title: Composable Service Layers
tour.description: Building on the frame types from Step 4, the network layers are composed with rama's Layer and Service pattern: TCP bytes become frames, and frames are routed to typed handlers. The input wrappers pair each value with a rama Extensions bag that carries per-connection data such as authentication state. The same layering is reused by the broker, the proxy and the clients. transaction_abortable.rs is a small example of a layer in this style: it rewrites TRANSACTION_ABORTABLE to INVALID_TXN_STATE in Produce responses for clients on Produce v10 or older.
tour.languageLesson: rama's Extensions store is Arc-backed, so cloning shares state and fork() creates an isolated child scope. Per-connection state is therefore inserted only once, and code must check whether it is already present.

tour.title: The Storage Abstraction
tour.description: The Storage and StorageFactory traits define the contract every backend must satisfy, along with shared domain types such as topitions, offsets, groups and transactions. A request/response channel service turns Storage calls into messages served against a real backend. Dispatch happens at runtime through factories rather than an enum, so the broker never depends on a concrete engine.
tour.languageLesson: Trait objects such as Arc<dyn StorageFactory> let the program pick an implementation at runtime from a URL scheme, while feature flags control which backends are compiled in.

tour.title: Pluggable Backends
tour.description: Each backend implements StorageFactory for its own URL scheme. dynostore covers memory://, s3:// and gs:// over an object store, nisshi-storage-sql covers postgres:// and sqlite://, and the null backend keeps only topic metadata. The Postgres DDL applied at broker startup shows the relational model behind topics, partitioned records and consumer groups.
tour.languageLesson: SQL schemas encode relationships through foreign keys and keys such as topic and partition. Applying the DDL at startup keeps a stateless broker's persistent state in the database.

tour.title: The Broker
tour.description: The Broker builder binds TCP listeners, registers itself with storage and wires the services together. service.rs assembles the rama stack of storage, coordinator and auth routes behind a FrameRouteService. The broker is generic over the Coordinator and Storage, and its node ID is fixed at 111 because the design is single-node and stateless.

tour.title: Groups and Authentication
tour.description: Consumer-group handling lives under the broker's group coordinator, with join, sync, heartbeat and offset handlers as separate modules. nisshi-auth adds SASL and SCRAM authentication through a per-connection state machine kept in the Extensions bag. Both plug into the service stack from Step 8. docs/consumer-groups.md explains consumer groups and committed offsets from the user side, with commands, timeouts and limits.

tour.title: Schemas and Lake Output
tour.description: nisshi-schema is the schema registry. It resolves Avro, JSON Schema and Protobuf schemas per topic and converts records to Arrow for Parquet, Iceberg and Delta tables. This is how schema-backed topics become lake tables, an optional extension of the storage story told in Steps 6 and 7.

tour.title: Proxy
tour.description: The proxy reuses the client and service layers from Step 5 to sit in front of another Kafka-compatible cluster. It wires TCP, frame, SASL-reject, topic-config and batching layers around an origin client. This shows how the same layered pattern is recombined for a different role.

tour.title: Testing and Fuzzing
tour.description: The broker's integration tests are one `it` binary that declares every test module. The fuzz crate round-trips encoded requests and responses to check that decoding is stable, and its targets run typed requests against an in-memory storage. Together these protect the generated codec and the service logic.

tour.title: Local Stack and Packaging
tour.description: compose.yaml starts the broker beside Postgres, MinIO, Grafana, Jaeger, Prometheus and the lakehouse catalog for local development. The Dockerfile packages a prebuilt static binary into a scratch image, with CA certificates and data directories prepared in an Alpine stage.
tour.languageLesson: A multi-stage Docker build uses a throwaway stage to prepare files and copies only the results into a minimal final image, which keeps the image small.

tour.title: CI Pipeline
tour.description: ci.yml is the main pipeline. It detects changes, runs fmt, clippy and tests, builds each storage engine, and runs compatibility legs against librdkafka and franz-go clients. It also produces the release binaries, tying every earlier layer to automated verification.
tour.languageLesson: GitHub Actions workflows declare triggers, jobs that run in parallel, and steps that run in order. Matrix builds repeat a job across variants such as storage engines.
